result.reply:
Two separate things going on here, and they matter differently.

First: is the gap real or just a "different route to the same place"? The plan's batching wasn't an implementation detail — the point of it was to bound memory. Loading everything at once doesn't get to that same guarantee by a different path, it drops the guarantee entirely. Small exports, nothing shows. Large one, you're OOMing where the plan specifically existed to prevent that. Passing the ticket's acceptance criteria doesn't cover this — those describe output correctness, not the memory behavior Marcus was actually solving for.

Second: nobody named it. If Riley had said "went with load-all instead of batching, here's why" — that's a build-time call I'd weigh on its merits. Nobody did, so right now it's just a diff quietly not matching the plan on the one property the plan cared about most. That's worth raising on its own, separate from whether the approach turns out to be defensible.

So this reads like a blocker to me, not a nitpick — but I haven't actually seen the diff yet, just your description of it. Before I land that as a real request-changes, I want the actual code (or at minimum the specific chunk handling the export/result-fetch) and Riley's reasoning if he has one — maybe there's a size cap upstream that makes this fine, maybe there isn't. Can you get me either?
